Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, I'm so worried about his eyes. He has hypermetropia, which means he's very far-sighted. I always make sure he wears his glasses when he's watching TV or playing games, and I remind his teachers to seat him at the front of the classroom.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes... he often asks people to repeat themselves because he doesn't catch what they say the first time. It's like he's not hearing everything clearly. I try to speak clearly and slowly when I talk to him.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing can be a challenge for him. He has trouble with harder foods like meat or crunchy vegetables. I try to cut his food into small pieces or cook it until it's softer.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: When he plays outside or runs around, he breathes faster than I expect. It worries me a little because I don't want him to overexert himself. I encourage him to take breaks and rest when he needs to.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He seems less coordinated than other kids his age. Like when he tries to ride a bike or climb on the playground equipment, he gets confused easily and loses balance. I hold his hand or provide support when we're out and about.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding was a big issue when he was a baby. He would spit up a lot and had reflux. Now it's better but sometimes after eating he still looks uncomfortable.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Well... his fontanelle took longer to close than it should have. That's why we went to see a specialist who kept an eye on it. Also‚ the doctor said something about the shape of his head and face being slightly different due to how his skull bones grew‚ but it doesn't seem to affect anything else.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing when exerting himself, which is a concern for potential overexertion.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, including spitting up and reflux, which has improved but still experiences discomfort after eating at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems less coordinated than other kids his age, gets confused easily, and loses balance, indicating potential neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves because he doesn't catch what they say the first time, indicating hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia (far-sightedness) and wears glasses, with his parents ensuring he sits at the front of the classroom to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble chewing harder foods and has difficulty with food texture, requiring food to be cut into small pieces or cooked until softer.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, necessitating regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's fontanelle took longer to close than expected, and there are concerns about the shape of his head and face due to skull bone growth, although it doesn't seem to affect anything else.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and many have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage hearing difficulties
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor and correct vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to assess heart condition
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis to monitor skeletal development
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioral needs.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Actually, yes. Our son often squints when he's trying to focus on things. It's been noticeable for a while now, and we're concerned it might be affecting his schoolwork.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He gets really frustrated in noisy environments. We've seen him cover his ears during fireworks or when there are too many kids screaming. It seems like the noise overwhelms him.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Cold foods and drinks make his teeth hurt. He complains about it often, especially after consuming ice cream or cold water. We're planning to take him to a dentist soon to get it checked.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: During playtime, his breathing gets faster than we expect. Not dangerously so, but it's enough to notice. We monitor it, but haven't had any alarming reports from his physical education classes.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, he was slower to sit up and walk compared to his peers. That was a concern early on, but with physiotherapy, he's caught up pretty well now.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Food textures are a big deal for him. He's extremely picky and will only eat certain types of food. We try to vary his diet, but it's challenging.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: His speech development is delayed. For his age, we expected more vocal interaction, but he's not saying as much as other kids his age. It's another thing we're keeping an eye on and considering speach therapy for.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely picky and has issues with food textures, which makes varying his diet challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was developmentally slower to sit up and walk compared to his peers, but with physiotherapy, he's caught up pretty well now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated in noisy environments and covers his ears, indicating potential hearing concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when trying to focus on things, which may be affecting his schoolwork.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth pain when consuming cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth pain and potential dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor potential vision problems
* Consideration of speech therapy to address delayed speech development
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and behavioural differences

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a hole in his heart.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky with food and won't eat certain things.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has low muscle tone and had something that is not finished yet (possibly referring to a neurological issue).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing problems and squints.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and some have speech delay.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Consider referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart condition that requires regular check-ups for monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, making mealtime challenging, and requires strategies to make eating easier.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally stares off into space for a few seconds, suggesting possible neurological episodes, and has difficulties with speech, including talking clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, and some may have developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in her ear, which is being monitored by doctors, and has speech delay, possibly linked to her hearing concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects her vision slightly, and is managed with glasses and regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, which can be treated with patching, exercises, glasses, or surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth pain, particularly with cold foods, and has large front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but possibly transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with speech and moves around differently than other kids her age, suggesting possible developmental delays or behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine, and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on the head or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and address any dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss and address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support the patient's development and address any delays or difficulties.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, and a small number require short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly during physical activity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have neurological issues such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat themselves, which may indicate a hearing issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience conductive hearing loss due to recurrent otitis media or glue ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on her teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often experience dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or have Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with clarity when trying to talk, and may have issues with attention or understanding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often experience developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may experience skeletal issues such as an unusual structure of the spinal bones, short fingers, or hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address the patient's weak enamel and potential dental concerns.
* Hearing reviews to assess and address any potential hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate and treat any vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's septal defect and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any potential skeletal issues.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioral concerns.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing certain sounds and frequently asks for the TV volume to be turned up, indicating potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, squints, and frequently rubs his eyes, indicating potential eyesight issues.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gains weight slowly and has challenging meal times due to eating very little at each sitting.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had fluid buildup in one ear, causing discomfort and affecting her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things far away and often squints or leans forward to get a better look.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems behind other children her age in many areas of development, including play, communication, and physical growth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth decay and prevent further problems
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor hearing loss and address any concerns
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and provide appropriate treatment

* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to address developmental delays and behavioral differences

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in her heart, requiring regular check-ups with a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation if her diet is not carefully managed, indicating gastrointestinal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring short-term or longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hypotonia, characterized by weaker muscles than typical for her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in some cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year, requiring treatment, and may have ongoing hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs her eyes frequently when trying to focus, suggesting vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is prone to cavities and requires more frequent dental visits than average, indicating dental concerns.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, necessitating regular dental check-ups, especially with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, which may require medication or therapeutic interventions.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than usual and stands and walks with a noticeably different posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly), curved 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to detect and manage hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile, to address potential growth hormone issues.

Parent: During physical activities like running or playing sports, he can't seem to keep up with his peers for very long. He gets tired easily and sometimes needs to sit down and rest, which is concerning because he's otherwise an active boy who loves to play outside.

Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Yes, there have been episodes where he stares off into space and doesn't respond immediately when we call his name. These episodes are brief but unsettling, and we're not sure what causes them or how to respond appropriately.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: He was diagnosed with hip dysplasia, which required some monitoring and physiotherapy to ensure proper development and prevent future complications. We're diligent about his follow-up appointments to keep track of his progress.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tends to turn the volume of the TV very high, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has difficulty seeing distant objects clearly.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular cardiac check-ups due to a potential heart condition, although currently, there's nothing to worry about.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties and can be picky with food, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with hypotonia, which means her muscles are a bit too stiff at times, and she does exercises at home to help loosen them up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to turn the volume up really high on the TV or her toys, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a habit of sitting way too close to the television or when reading books, indicating potential eyesight problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth compared to other kids her age, which affects her speech a little bit.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a noticeably different posture when standing or walking, which may be related to her hypotonia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and address any potential eyesight problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and address any potential heart issues.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioral differences.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if the patient's height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consideration of a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess the patient's skeletal development.

## 1) RESPIRATORY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a pre-existing heart condition that requires regular monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has slower weight gain and requires a adjusted diet to ensure proper growth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with a tethered cord that affects his lower back and legs, requiring ongoing monitoring and occasional physiotherapy sessions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year, which affected his hearing temporarily, and has required medication to clear the fluid build-up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often says things look a bit fuzzy to him, and he squints when looking at distant objects or watching TV.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty chewing tougher foods and finds it hard to chew.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which affects his posture and requires regular checks, and undescended testes that are being investigated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and may have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing
* Eyesight review to monitor vision
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor spinal health
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Regular monitoring of tethered cord and adjustment of physiotherapy sessions as needed

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart, but it is being managed with regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is quite picky with food textures, which can make mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily when playing outside, more so than his friends.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: There's fluid in his ear, and they're waiting for it to clear up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV or books, which makes his parents worry about his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: Cold foods make his teeth sensitive, so they try to avoid those.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves a bit differently compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delays.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient moves a bit differently compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and may have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the structural issue with the heart
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) if clinical concerns arise

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences unpredictable bowel movements, managed through diet adjustments and close monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome may have feeding difficulties, and a small number require longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient took longer to achieve certain developmental milestones like walking and sitting, but once started, progressed well.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks for repetitions due to not catching what was said the first time, especially with background noise or in a hurry.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, and many require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is myopic, having trouble seeing things far away, noticeable since preschool.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to cavities due to weak enamel, requiring diligent oral hygiene and regular dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth and may experience other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes more time to hit developmental targets than typically expected, under observation by the healthcare team.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and requires observation for achieving milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage weak enamel and prevent cavities.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis to monitor the septal defect.
* Consider skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... she has myopia, which means she can't see things far away very clearly. It's been really tough for her in school because she struggles to read the board unless she's right up close. I worry it might affect her learning if we don't get the right glasses for her.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There's fluid in her ear, and it's caused her a lot of discomfort and pain. The pediatrician said it's pretty common but still needs to be treated so it doesn't lead to more serious issues like hearing loss. I just want to make sure she gets the best care possible.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth are very weak, the enamel is almost nonexistent. We have to be super careful about what she eats and drinks, no sugary snacks or acidic foods. I feel like I'm always worrying about her teeth, it's exhausting but I know it's necessary.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: She can't seem to keep up with the other kids when they play. Even simple games like tag leave her out of breath and she gets tired easily. I fear it might be something more serious with her heart, maybe it's not pumping properly? I just want what's best for her.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Yes... hypotonia. Her muscles are too stiff sometimes, and it affects her movement. She has trouble walking or running like other children her age. It breaks my heart to see her struggle so much.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been a nightmare. She refuses certain foods and has trouble swallowing others. Some days are better than others, but it's a constant source of stress for me. I just wish she could eat normally like other kids.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: She has scoliosis, which is a curvature of the spine. The doctors say it's mild for now but needs monitoring to ensure it doesn't worsen over time. I'm terrified of what might happen if it progresses, the thought of her in pain or discomfort keeps me up at night.
report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness and shortness of breath during physical activities, suggesting possible cardiac issues that may be related to the syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Cardiac issues, including changes to heart valves, holes in heart chambers, and structural changes, are reported in approximately 38% of individuals with KBG syndrome, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, including refusal of certain foods and trouble swallowing, which is a source of stress for the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties are common, with some individuals requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding, and a very small number needing longer-term tube feeding due to lack of interest in feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, characterized by stiff muscles, affecting movement and causing difficulty with walking or running.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Neurological issues, including developmental delay, seizures (in approximately 20-40% of individuals), and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ADHD, are common.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in her ear, causing discomfort and pain, and potentially leading to hearing loss if not treated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, is a significant concern, with many individuals requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, making it difficult to see things far away, which affects her learning in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, are more common, with treatment options including glasses, patching, exercises, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has very weak teeth with almost nonexistent enamel, requiring careful management of diet and regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including large front teeth, weak enamel, and other issues, are common, necessitating regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's myopia affects her ability to learn in school, as she struggles to read the board unless close to it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream schools and others benefiting from special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety, are common, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, a mild curvature of the spine that requires monitoring to prevent worsening.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), are seen in some individuals, with a small number having hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's weak teeth.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to address the fluid in the ear and prevent hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct the patient's myopia and prevent learning difficulties.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to investigate the patient's heart condition.
* Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor the patient's scoliosis and prevent worsening.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support the patient's development and manage symptoms.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away, such as the board in her classroom, and needs to sit closer to see what's going on.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is managed with regular check-ups and medication, allowing him to engage in physical activities without significant limitations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences bowel problems from time to time, which are noticeable and uncomfortable for him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome, with a very small number requiring longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted quicker than his peers during playtime or when running around, and there is a mention of delayed fontanelle closure, which may have long-term effects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, and some may have tethered cord, leading to pain, weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes does not respond right away when called, suggesting possible hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, corrected with glasses, and no other vision problems are mentioned.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than usual, which could lead to orthodontic issues later on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, necessitating regular dental check-ups, especially with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) in secondary school due to the extra demands.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind his peers, and there are concerns about his energy levels and endurance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with some requiring medication or behavioural therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: There is a mention of delayed fontanelle closure, which may have long-term skeletal effects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers (brachydactyly), curved 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and an increased risk of scoliosis, hip dysplasia, and delayed closure of the soft spot on the head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address orthodontic issues and weak enamel.
* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage any hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct and manage myopia and monitor for other vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to manage the septal defect.
* Consider skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support developmental and behavioural challenges.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when playing outside, which may be related to a potential heart condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, including spitting up and crying during feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient stares sometimes, which may be related to a potential neurological issue, such as seizures, which affect around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are at risk of seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has otitis media and requires ear drops and follow-up check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints when looking at things, which may be related to a vision problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental check-ups and has been advised to take care of her teeth to prevent future problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient talks late, which may be related to a developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school and may need special educational support.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including delayed talking.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental problems
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing and increased heart rate during playtime, which may indicate a potential respiratory or cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's heart rate increases more than expected during active play, and the parent has noticed faster breathing, which may be related to a cardiac condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, which can be managed through diet and hydration.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has episodes of staring off into space, which may be indicative of a neurological issue, such as seizures or absence seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some may have difficulty with speech development and learning.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has otitis media, which has caused issues with his hearing, and a squint that affects his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint that affects his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, which requires careful management to prevent further problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis and hip dysplasia, which require monitoring and management to ensure they don't affect his mobility or cause unnecessary discomfort.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor and manage the patient's hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor and manage the patient's squint and vision
* Cardiac review to investigate the patient's faster heart rate and breathing during playtime
* Referral for a skeletal review to monitor and manage the patient's scoliosis and hip dysplasia

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has astigmatism, which affects her vision. She sees things slightly blurred at times and has trouble focusing on close objects. We've had her glasses prescribed to help correct this.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: There seems to be an issue with her hearing; she can pick up some sounds without difficulty, but struggles with others. It's as if she's not registering certain frequencies or volumes. This has been noticeable in both quiet and noisy environments.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her front teeth are noticeably larger than those of her peers. This has been a concern for us, especially in terms of aesthetics and potential orthodontic interventions down the line.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: She tires easily during physical activities. Even simple tasks like running around in the playground or climbing stairs leave her breathless and needing rest. This limitation on physical endurance is concerning and impacts her ability to participate fully in school sports and play.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: She gets exhausted quickly when engaging in physical activities. This isn't just about cardiovascular endurance; it seems there's a neurologicall component where her brain and muscles don't seem to coordinate as efficiently as they should.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Bowel movements have been irregular. There are times when she experiences constipation, and at others, she has diarrhea. Managing her diet has become essential to try and regulate these issues.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Despite being 8 years old, her speech development is delayed. She doesn't articulate as many words or express herself as clearly as children of the same age. This has been another significant concern for us.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences irregular bowel movements, with periods of constipation and diarrhea, requiring dietary management.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and gastrointestinal issues, including lack of interest in feeding, can be significant and long-lasting in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits neurological issues, including easy exhaustion during physical activities, suggesting a potential neurologic component affecting coordination and endurance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Neurological issues, including seizures in approximately 20-40% of individuals, can be a feature of KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing issues, struggling with certain frequencies or volumes, indicating potential conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, is a common feature in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, affecting her vision with blurry sight and trouble focusing on close objects, corrected with glasses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, are more common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably larger front teeth than her peers, a common feature of KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns, including large front teeth and weak enamel, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream schools and others requiring special education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has delayed speech development, not articulating as many words or expressing herself as clearly as peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder and ADHD, are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curvature of the 5th fingers, and spinal issues, can be features of KBG syndrome.

* Hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct and manage vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess cardiac function.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support development and manage symptoms.

report:
# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect in his heart that was diagnosed early on. Regular cardiology check-ups help monitor the situation and adjust treatment as necessary to ensure it doesn't impact his daily life too significantly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some may require surgery, while others just need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had trouble feeding due to reflux and digestive discomfort as an infant. However, those issues resolved themselves over time and now his eating habits are mostly normal.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects muscle tone and can make movements slightly more difficult. Physical therapy sessions have been very helpful in managing this condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types. Seizures typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media when he was younger, but after treatment and follow-up care, the condition cleared up and hasn't caused any lasting issues with his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple aeration tube (grommet) insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which affects his ability to focus on objects directly in front of him. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak tooth enamel, and as a result, extra precautions have been taken to prevent decay and strengthen them through fluoride treatments and good oral hygiene practices.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has taken longer to reach developmental milestones than peers, but with support and therapies, he's making steady progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has taken longer to reach developmental milestones than peers, but with support and therapies, he's making steady progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than typical for his age group.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage weak tooth enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for any hearing loss
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiology check-ups to monitor the septal defect in the heart
* Physical therapy sessions to manage hypotonia
* Monitoring of growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed
